meta.title: Selekoa historical research sample
meta.scope: Selected historical records, 1965–2024, plus prior roles with unknown dates. Genesis source checks are dated 2026-09-17; personnel-continuity checks are dated 2026-09-18. Human source review pending. Not a current or comprehensive sector inventory. Governance version histories through July 2026, researched September 18, 2026; policy text is not evidence of implementation. Selected capital and compute records through April 2026; transaction stages do not imply current arrangements or realised spending. Targeted corrections dated 2026-09-25: one attributed claim accepted after explicit human source review; a second narrowly scoped résumé passage is human-reviewed. Other seed claims remain pending. Intellectual Lineage II adds selected oversight citations and agenda reception, checked 2026-09-25; all new records remain pending human review. Evaluation Institutions I adds bounded institutional and documentary records, checked 2026-09-27; new claims remain seeds, not editorially accepted. Evaluation Ontology I adds four scoped engagement and institutional announcement seeds, checked 2026-09-28; no human acceptance or legal succession inferred. Schema 2.7 records each source's language; the frontier safety framework sources also record the nearest existing Internet Archive capture, checked 2026-10-03. A capture shows only what the archive held on its date and does not authenticate earlier bytes. Schema 2.8 adds quoted framework provisions, recorded absences, provision-level changes and the first contested assessments to the frontier safety frameworks collection, together with Meta and Microsoft framework families, checked 2026-10-03; provisions describe what editions state, not implementation. Schema 2.9 adds control-structure and external-commitment records; its first topic, California SB 53 as chaptered (enactment, 19 quoted provisions and four framework editions that link themselves to it in their own words), was checked 2026-10-04. A commitment or legal obligation is never evidence of compliance, and no record states that the statute applies to a named company. Schema 2.10 records assessments as questions posed by Selekoa rather than statements of a source, and dates an assessment by what it assesses, never by the publication window of its sources (corrected 2026-10-05). Schema 2.11 adds propositions and the first human-thought collection: located texts from 1863 to 2022 that articulate, contest or bear on propositions about machine intelligence, each with its role and register, checked 2026-10-06. "Earliest located" means the earliest text found by the recorded searches; no record claims a first use, an origin or an influence. Schema 2.12 adds a collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s documented arguments about common claims on advanced AI, 1996–2026: dated passages that state, contest or bear on 29 generically phrased propositions, with engagement, retrospective reports and context-only passages marked, admitted 2026-10-08 from a machine-prepared and machine-audited candidate pack. A record says what a text states, not whether it is right. The 2026-10-10 frontier-governance increment adds selected provisions of the EU AI Act as published in 2024 and of the 2026 Digital Omnibus amendments that bear on general-purpose AI model providers, and the New York RAISE Act as announced by the Governor; checked 2026-10-10, new claims remain seeds, not editorially accepted, and Regulation texts describe duties, not compliance. The 2026-10-11 frontier-governance increment adds Commission guidelines, the training-content template, further chapters of the EU Code, a draft implementing regulation on proceedings, the New York Chapter 96 text and a Chinese generative-AI measure; checked 2026-10-11, new claims remain seeds, not editorially accepted, and texts describe duties, not compliance. Schema 2.13 adds a collection on the economics of machine intelligence: dated passages from 1952 to 2024 that state, contest or bear on 19 generically phrased propositions about explosive growth and about how mainstream economics treated automation and AI, with each text’s source tier, model conditions and stated estimates, admitted 2026-10-14 from two machine-prepared, machine-audited and cross-family-checked candidate packs. A record says what a text states, not whether an argument or model is right. Schema 2.14 adds structured author names to sources for citation export, 2026-10-15: a cataloguing aid for splitting personal names, not evidence about anyone’s name. On 2026-10-16 the economics collection gained a third strand, admitted from a machine-prepared, machine-audited and cross-family-checked candidate pack: dated passages from 1998 to 2026 in which economists and economics venues state, contest or bear on five propositions about recursive self-improvement, superintelligence, existential risk from AI, developers’ incentives and economics’ own engagement with these ideas; a record says what a text states, not whether an argument or model is right. On 2026-10-17 the maintainer's disposition of two cross-family machine checks revised nine proposition records in the Yudkowsky and human-thought collections; all remain seeds. Schema 2.15 adds the lab genealogy, admitted on 2026-10-17 from a machine-prepared, machine-audited and cross-family-checked candidate pack: dated records of who founded, led, joined and left frontier AI labs from 2010 to 2026, with organisations’ stated founding dates, licensing-and-hiring agreements and disbanded units; a reason is recorded only where the person or organisation concerned stated it, many records rest on reporting, and coverage is selective. Schema 2.16 lets a collection withhold an earliest-located role, by a recorded decision, while a lead is checked. On 2026-10-25 the maintainer’s adjudication of a same-family and a cross-family machine re-check corrected the economics collection: one text re-tiered, six proposition records added, five earliest-located roles moved and one withheld; qualifications in other collections were reworded and one framework absence narrowed. All records remain seeds. On 2026-10-26 the maintainer’s adjudication of a reader test and a same-family machine re-check corrected two document credits in the economics collection, one compute qualification and one evidence locator. All records remain seeds. Also on 2026-10-26, by the maintainer’s decision, five lab genealogy records held back for want of a second retrieval of Adept’s 2022 launch post were admitted on a cross-family machine check’s read of an archive capture, and one Stargate quotation was extended; all remain seeds. Schema 2.17 adds the framework comparison, admitted on 2026-10-27 from a machine-prepared, machine-audited, cross-family-checked and adjudicated candidate pack: for six edition-neutral questions on required actions, who decides and exceptions, one record per framework edition and question, either quoting what the edition states (with “stated, partly” where a passage has what the question asks for only in a weaker form) or recording that no passage was found within a stated search. A record says what an edition states, not whether it was implemented or complied with, and a shared question does not make two provisions equivalent. The author-person admission of 2026-10-27 adds person records for credited authors of texts that the proposition collections study, and one authorship record per credited text, each quoting the name as printed (or, for three Turing typescripts, the archive catalogue’s attribution). The records come from a machine-prepared candidate pack checked blind by a reviewer from a different model family; no person has reviewed them. An authorship record is a credit, not sole authorship, priority, agreement, affiliation or influence. Schema 2.18 adds the comparison’s twelve further questions, on risk domains, thresholds, evaluation timing, reporting and revision, from the same pack: each stated cell gives an explicit paraphrase of the edition’s passage with its page instead of a quotation, so that no edition exceeds the quotation limit. On 2026-10-27 a second collection of Chinese frontier-AI institutional histories was admitted from a machine-prepared, machine-audited and cross-family-checked candidate pack, with the maintainer’s decisions of that date: model releases, licences, technical-report authorship and documented investors of Moonshot AI, MiniMax, Baidu (ERNIE) and ByteDance Seed, and what three Chinese AI governance texts state — the AI Safety Governance Framework of TC260 (versions 1.0 to 3.0), the AI Industry Alliance’s AI Safety Commitments with their 17 initially listed companies, and Shanghai AI Laboratory’s Frontier AI Risk Management Framework. Chinese passages are quoted in Chinese with machine translations; a listing is not a signature or compliance, and a framework or licence states terms, not implementation. All records remain seeds. On 2026-10-28, by the maintainer’s decisions of 2026-10-27, a blind cross-family re-check of Meta’s Frontier AI Framework v1.1 against the archive capture of 2025-02-13 confirmed its four comparison cells recorded earlier and supplied thirteen further cells, three of them by decisions of 2026-10-28. Katja Grace’s two authorship records were admitted on an identifying source checked by the same reviewer family, and three document records now say which source gives which date. All records remain seeds.
